source.title: [PROPOSAL] RFP-022 — Sovereign Bridge (also covers RFP-021)
source.body:
This proposal also covers **RFP-021 — Trustless Ethereum State Attestation for LEZ (Tier M)**, in addition to RFP-022, per Logos forum guidance (6 November 2026): combined bids submit one proposal, select RFP-022 in the RFP ID dropdown, state RFP-021 coverage at the top, and provide milestones for each.

### RFP ID

RFP-022 — Privacy-Preserving Wrapped ERC-20 and Ether Bridge for LEZ

### Your Project Name

Sovereign Bridge

### Team or Organization Name

ZaSourceCode (GitHub @YodHeVauHe), Foundation Stone Algorithms

### Primary Contact

GitHub @YodHeVauHe · X @zasourcecode · foundationstonealgorithms.shop

### Team Members

Member 1
Name or pseudonym: ZaSourceCode (GitHub @YodHeVauHe)
Social links: https://github.com/YodHeVauHe · https://x.com/zasourcecode · https://foundationstonealgorithms.shop
Role: Solo technical lead — architecture, LEZ/Logos integration, product delivery, documentation, and coordination of specialist contributors
Status: Full-time for this engagement

Recruitment plan (no named specialists yet — will be contracted before Milestone 2 starts):
- Ethereum light-client / BLS12-381 / sync-committee contributor for RFP-021 consensus verification (reuse assessment of r0vm-helios / Helios and in-program BLS path).
- Zero-knowledge / RISC0 proof-system contributor for LEZ-side proving and the LEZ→Ethereum succinct burn proof path.
- Solidity / EVM vault contributor for the escrow contract, USDT-style non-boolean transfers, immutable verifier wiring, and audit readiness.

Specialists will be credited as contractors in milestone reports. Core ownership, integration, Logos modules, SPEL IDL, mini-app/CLI, and acceptance against hard requirements remain with the technical lead.

### Project Summary

Sovereign Bridge is a combined proposal for RFP-021 and RFP-022: a reusable trustless Ethereum state attestation primitive for LEZ, plus a privacy-preserving lock-and-mint bridge that consumes it.

RFP-021 delivers an application-free LEZ module that runs an Ethereum light client in-program, verifies sync-committee finality and inclusion (account, storage slot, event log), evaluates predicates, and emits chain-bound verified statements with deterministic identifiers for consumer nullifiers. Updates are permissionless; submitters are liveness-only.

RFP-022 builds the bridge on that primitive: a Solidity vault escrows registered ERC-20s and native ETH; a LEZ program mints one-to-one wrapped assets after attestation; burns release on Ethereum via native cryptographic verification of the LEZ burn. Deposits and burns do not publish opposite-chain destinations. Fixed denominations, delayed claims, and permissionless relayers are the privacy baseline. Recovery of unclaimed deposits and unreleased burns is from existing wallet credentials and chain state only.

Duration: 20 weeks. Licence: MIT + Apache 2.0. Output: testnet implementation on LEZ testnet 0.4 and a public Ethereum testnet, with cost measurement, adversarial tests, Logos core module, mini-app, CLI/daemon, SPEL IDL, and an independent security audit included in budget.

### Technical Approach

**Architecture.** Five components: (1) RFP-021 Ethereum state attestation LEZ program; (2) RFP-022 Solidity vault; (3) RFP-022 LEZ bridge program consuming attestation statements; (4) privacy/proof layer (fixed denominations, delayed claims, nullifiers, destination-bound claims, succinct LEZ burn proof for Ethereum release); (5) Logos core module, mini-app, headless CLI/daemon, SPEL IDL.

**RFP-021 path.** Assess reuse of mature light-client implementations (including r0vm-helios / Helios) before rewriting. Shared consensus tracking vs per-consumer inclusion/predicate evaluation. Permissionless updates with need-check and varied deferral so gas cost does not always fall on the fastest operator. Chain ID binding; immutable verification logic (no mutable ProgramId swap); instance replacement rather than in-place checkpoint mutation when outside weak subjectivity.

**RFP-022 path.** Vault supports USDC, USDT, DAI, WETH, and native ETH (no forced WETH wrap); handles non-boolean ERC-20 transfers. Mint/burn to private or public LEZ accounts (UI defaults private). Admin authority (RFP-001) for registry/caps/fees/finality; freeze authority (RFP-002) independently on each leg. Multi-entity independent configurations with strict separation. Consume RFP-021 for inbound verification; do not rebuild consensus verification inside the bridge.

**Hard-requirement design commitments (to be delivered, not claimed as already done):**
- Trust assumptions document: honest sync-committee supermajority and attack cost; weak-subjectivity checkpoint supplier and independent verification via the Logos Ethereum core module API; what attestations prove/do not prove; off-chain roles as liveness-only.
- Checkpoint / weak subjectivity: written at instance init and never rewritten; stale instances replaced by fresh init; consumer migration documented.
- Fee structure: configurable protocol fees on LEZ mint and burn (wrapped token, native LEZ, or mix); fee values must not fingerprint transactions; admin can set either fee to zero; denomination, rate range, collection point, and routing documented at Milestone 1.
- Finality defaults: admin-configurable depths both ways; recommend concrete defaults in Milestone 1 with residual reorg risk; depth changes must not invalidate already-valid claims.
- Admin / freeze: RFP-001 registry and caps; RFP-002 global and per-token pause on vault and LEZ program independently.
- Failsafe (RFP-022 Security #9): recovery path for in-flight deposits/burns after a discovered verification vulnerability that still requires the rightful party to prove entitlement — never admin redirection of funds. If no mechanism meeting those constraints is achievable, Milestone 1 will document why and what happens to affected funds instead.
- Privacy: document residual correlations (amount/timing/fee-payer); default private path; error paths must not reveal which deposit/burn failed.

**Testing / performance.** CI e2e round trips; adversarial fabricated-chain and replay suites; cycle/gas/proof-time/proof-size measurements per RFP-020 methodology; anonymity-set reporting; storage growth projections.

### Milestones, Payout and Timeline

Milestone 1 — Protocol design and feasibility (Shared: RFP-021 + RFP-022)
Payout: $8,000
Duration: Weeks 1–3
Deliverables: system architecture; FURPS requirements mapping for both RFPs; threat model and trust-assumptions outline; light-client reuse assessment plan; privacy/anonymity-set model; fee structure and finality-default recommendations; failsafe approach decision; architecture decision log; specialist contributor sourcing kicked off.

Milestone 2 — Ethereum state attestation (RFP-021)
Payout: $16,000
Duration: Weeks 4–8
Deliverables: light-client integration; sync-committee / finality / handoff verification; inclusion proofs (account, storage, log); predicate interface; deterministic statement IDs; chain binding; permissionless update tooling with need-check and deferral; LEZ attestation program on testnet 0.4; reference consumer sketches.

Milestone 3 — Ethereum vault and LEZ bridge core (RFP-022)
Payout: $16,000
Duration: Weeks 6–12 (overlaps M2)
Deliverables: Solidity vault (ERC-20 + native ETH + USDT-style transfers); token registry via admin authority; LEZ bridge mint/burn; nullifier uniqueness keyed on attestation statement ID; decimal normalization; caps; freeze wiring; private and public account support; testnet deploys.

Milestone 4 — Privacy and redemption proofs (RFP-022)
Payout: $14,000
Duration: Weeks 9–15
Deliverables: fixed-denomination claims; delayed claim path; destination-bound proofs; succinct LEZ burn proof and Ethereum-side immutable verification; permissionless relayer integration; seed-based position recovery; privacy leakage analysis.

Milestone 5 — Integration, testing and performance (Shared)
Payout: $10,000
Duration: Weeks 13–18
Deliverables: full Ethereum↔LEZ round trip; e2e and adversarial CI; reorg/finality tests; RFP-021 and RFP-022 cost measurements; storage-growth analysis; recovery tests; hard-requirement ↔ test matrix.

Milestone 6 — Release and documentation (Shared)
Payout: $6,000
Duration: Weeks 19–20
Deliverables: Logos core module; mini-app (private-by-default UX); CLI/daemon; SPEL IDL; module catalog release; developer, operator, and deployer docs; trust assumptions and privacy docs; design decision log current; audit-ready codebase under MIT + Apache 2.0.

Milestone 7 — Independent security audit (Shared; included in budget)
Payout: $10,000
Duration: Scheduled after M5/M6 readiness (audit firm lead time excluded from the 20-week build estimate where the firm’s calendar requires it; remediation within engagement)
Deliverables: third-party audit of RFP-021 consensus/inclusion verification and RFP-022 vault + bridge verification paths; published report; remediation of findings to Logos acceptance.

### Total Requested Budget (USD)

$80,000

### Relevant Experience

Solo lead: ZaSourceCode / GitHub @YodHeVauHe / Foundation Stone Algorithms. Relevant owned public work in the Logos / LEZ ecosystem:

- https://github.com/YodHeVauHe/logos-osm — LP-0018 OpenStreetMap integration (SPEL/LEZ registry, SDK, CLI, Basecamp module; Rust; MIT OR Apache-2.0)
- https://github.com/YodHeVauHe/logos-osm-modules — module catalog packaging for logos-osm
- https://github.com/YodHeVauHe/lez-wallet — LEZ Wallet and Provider SDK (λPrize LP-0021): public/private accounts, tokens, dApp connect, CLI
- https://github.com/YodHeVauHe/logos-forum — LP-0026 forum app with uid/alias/anonymous/rotating identity
- https://github.com/YodHeVauHe/logos-mobile — Android platform for running Logos infrastructure locally (Rust)
- https://github.com/YodHeVauHe/AuditChain — tamper-evident trust layer for institutional auditing
- https://github.com/YodHeVauHe/TokenWork — commission-based token platform

Honest gap: among 231 public repositories under @YodHeVauHe there is no owned public Ethereum light client, BLS sync-committee verifier, RISC0 consensus guest, or Solidity bridge vault. Public forks of upstream projects are not cited as authored work. Those specialties will be covered by contracted contributors under the recruitment plan above, with reuse of audited libraries (e.g. r0vm-helios / Helios / mature RISC0 stacks) assessed in Milestone 1.

### Post-Delivery Plan

ZaSourceCode / Foundation Stone Algorithms will maintain Sovereign Bridge for **12 months after Milestone 6 acceptance** at no extra cost beyond the grant: security reports acknowledged within 48 hours; critical correctness bugs patched on a best-effort basis; documentation and module-catalog release kept installable for Logos clients; reasonable integration questions answered via the GitHub issue/PR for the delivery repo. After that window, maintenance is best-effort open-source unless a follow-on agreement is negotiated. Handoff materials (deployer docs, trust assumptions, decision log, SPEL IDL, and operator runbooks) are written so any independent party can operate an instance without the original team. Mainnet deployment remains out of scope per the RFPs and is the responsibility of whoever deploys.

### Permissions and Consent

- [X] I/We confirm Logos may contact me using the primary contact information provided above for follow-ups and next steps.
- [ ] I/We consent to Logos using information from this proposal publicly such as blogs case studies social posts or analytical reporting. Rededs can be requested at any time.

### Program Requirements

- [X] I/We have read and agree to the Logos RFP Terms and Conditions and I understand that no Grant is awarded and no right to payment arises unless a Grant Agreement is executed.
- [X] I/We understand that RFP specifications are proposals rather than instructions, that Logos makes no representations as to their legal or regulatory treatment, and that we are responsible for assessing what we build, deploy or operate and for complying with the laws that apply to us.
- [X] I/We understand this project must be open-sourced under the MIT and Apache 2.0 Licenses unless explicitly approved otherwise.
- [X] I/We are prepared to deliver milestone-based outcomes.
